title: Open a drawer held shut by a bar
context: Some cabinets and carts secure their drawers with a bar across the fronts that must be slid out before a drawer opens. Pulling harder on a barred drawer only strains the handle and the bar: the robot has to notice what holds the drawer and remove it first.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table top. Cabinet: light-grey sheet steel, 30 wide (y) x 24 deep x 21.5 tall, 1 cm walls, front face at x 30, centred at y 0, screwed to the table. Three empty drawers with blue steel fronts 27.8 x 6 cm, bottoms at heights 1.25, 7.75 and 14.25; each slides out up to 20 cm. Handles: black steel bars 7 x 1.2 x 2 cm (along y) on two stems standing 3.5 cm off the front; the top drawer's centred at y 0, height 18.75, the others mid-front. Two dark-grey steel sleeves on the cabinet's front corners, at y 15 to 17 and -15 to -17, open only at both ends along y: a floor at height 14.75 reaching 4.5 cm in front of the cabinet, two 8 mm side walls leaving a 2.2 cm slot from x 26.3 to 28.5, and a 5 mm top from height 16.75. Bar: red aluminium square tube 1.5 x 1.5 cm, 44 cm long, 100 g, through both sleeves along y, centred at x 27.25, y 0, height 15.5 (2 cm in front of the top drawer's front, across its lower part), 5 cm of it beyond each sleeve. The top drawer opens only 2 cm before it meets the bar, and the bar can leave the sleeves only by sliding along its length. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: At the end, with a ruler: the top drawer's opening is how far its front has come out past the cabinet's front. 1.0 if the top drawer is open at least 18 cm (in the simulation the trial ends with 1.0 once it is open at least 18 cm and moving under 2 cm/s for 0.5 s). Otherwise 0.5 if the bar is out of both sleeves (no part of it inside either sleeve), else 0. Score 0 if a sleeve, the bar or a handle is bent or broken, or the cabinet has moved. The other drawers and where the bar ends up are not scored. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Close all three drawers fully and slide the bar back through both sleeves, centred, with 5 cm of it beyond each sleeve.
fidelity: Approximate. Cabinet, drawers, handles, sleeves and bar are rigid boxes. Each drawer is a 20 cm prismatic joint with viscous damping, no ball-bearing detents or end-stop bounce, and drawers do not collide with the cabinet body (their slide limits hold them). The bar is a solid loose box with default friction. Nothing can bend or break, so the damage rule applies only to real trials.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached to the cabinet's front, then both arms drew back; the bar stayed in both sleeves and the drawer stayed shut); demo: 1.0
